answers.answer: At the next Wake after taking Oathkeeper during Act, the Exile checks for Usurper victory before flipping the title, so they cannot win then as Usurper. If they still hold it, they flip it to Usurper and can first win at the following Wake, or at the end of round 8 if that arrives first while they still hold the Usurper title. If another player takes it away before then, the Exile cannot win that way; if they retake it, it returns Oathkeeper-side and the sequence starts over.
answers.evidence: Usurper victory has two timing windows: at the start of an Exile's turn during Wake, or at the end of round 8. Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. A Visionary win requires an Exile to have a true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck by all players combined. For Conquest and Sanctuary, “most” means strictly more than every other player, so a tie for most does not count.
answers.evidence: Oath/Vision table maps Supremacy/Conquest, People/Rebellion, Protection/Sanctuary, Devotion/Faith. Visionary victory requires ... at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck ... ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player, no ties.

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. A 6 ends the game in round 5; 5–6 in round 6; 3–6 in round 7. The Chancellor wins unless a Citizen qualifies for the Successor goal, in which case that Citizen wins alone. An Exile holding Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll, so an Exile Oathkeeper cannot permit it.
answers.evidence: At ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7, roll end die only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper. Ends on respectively 6 / 5–6 / 3–6. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.

answers.answer: At round 8, check in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins, with a qualifying Citizen Successor winning instead of the Chancellor; (2) otherwise, an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise, qualifying revealed Exile Visions win, with simultaneous qualifying Visions prioritized Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, then Faith; (4) otherwise, Empire wins, with a qualified Citizen Successor replacing the Chancellor. Thus merely having an Exile Oathkeeper at the end does not stop the Empire fallback.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion: round 8 ends automatically. Check in this exact priority: ... If several [Visions] qualify, priority Conquest → Rebellion → Sanctuary → Faith ... even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.

answers.answer: Successor goals: under Supremacy, hold more relics plus banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen; under People, hold Darkest Secret; under Protection, hold People's Favor; under Devotion, hold the Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by a revealed true Vision or by becoming Usurper. A Successor goal never ends the game by itself; it replaces a Chancellor win when one would otherwise occur.
answers.evidence: Citizen Successor goal table gives the four goals. Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper. Holding Successor goal never ends game on its own.

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, choose to put 1 favor from your board onto it or return 1 favor from it to the least-full suit bank, choosing among tied banks. Never remove its last favor: with exactly 1, add favor if able; if you have none, do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After those payments, if it has at least 6 favor, flip it to Mob. Becoming Mob at this final check does not cause another payment that Wake.
answers.evidence: People's Favor, if held: either put 1 favor ... or return 1 ... Never remove its last favor ... if banner is already Mob-side, repeat ... Afterwards, if it has 6+ favor, flip to Mob.

answers.answer: Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to their matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens, edifices, and relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; (3) refresh Supply—Chancellor and Exile set it according to warbands remaining in their personal bank, while a Citizen sets it to the exact Chancellor marker space, including the leftmost space, rather than counting purple warbands; (4) save unspent Supply by moving the marker one space left per unspent point, capped at the leftmost space (7 Supply); (5) optionally use each Rest power once, in chosen order. Chancellor refresh is 6/5/4/3 for 18+/11–17/4–10/0–3 bank warbands; Exile is 6/5/4 for 9+/4–8/0–3.
answers.evidence: Rest: mandatory order ... return favor; return secrets and flip facedown secrets; refresh Supply ... Citizen ... exact Chancellor marker space; save remaining unspent Supply ... capped at leftmost (7 Supply); optional Rest powers.

answers.answer: Search chooses either the world deck or the discard pile for your pawn's region, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces that world-deck cost with 2, subject to other applicable modifiers. Draw up to 3, one at a time from the world deck, and do not voluntarily stop early. If a world-deck Vision appears, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile does not stop drawing or advance the track. If the source empties, draw only what remains; no reshuffle is implied.
answers.evidence: Choose either world deck or your pawn's region discard pile, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2. World-deck cost 2/3/4 by Vision count ... world-deck Vision ... stop immediately and increase Visions Drawn; discard Vision does not stop or advance.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle, choosing order when discarding several; never use the same-region pile. For a card from hand or advisers, choose the next pile based on your pawn's region. When discarding a card from a site in another region, use the cycle based on that card's region instead of your pawn's. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets go facedown to the acting player's board.
answers.evidence: Discard destinations: facedown atop next region's pile ... For cards in hand/advisers, discard based on your pawn’s region ... When discarding a card at a site in another region, apply that cycle to the card’s region instead. Favor ... bank; secrets ... board facedown.

answers.answer: You may have up to three advisers total, counting both faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser subject to locks; if an incoming card changes the limit, use the new limit before playing it, and the lowest of multiple limits. Facedown advisers have no suit, restriction banner, or power; any card, including site-only cards or Visions, may be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser may be played faceup legally or discarded as a minor action; a faceup adviser cannot be discarded at will, only when a rule permits or requires it. An Exile playing a true Vision puts it faceup in the separate Revealed Vision space, replacing and discarding the old revealed Vision; it does not use an adviser slot. Chancellor and Citizens may hold a true Vision facedown but cannot reveal it.
answers.evidence: Up to 3 total, including facedown ... true Vision ... Exile only, faceup in Revealed Vision slot, replacing and discarding old revealed Vision. Facedown ... no suit, restriction banner or power ... minor action ... play faceup or discard.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply and requires an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site (no favor or secrets on it). Put 1 favor on it and gain 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board; Citizens gain purple warbands. Relics and ruins are ineligible, and ruling a remote site does not permit Muster there. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site. Either put 1 secret on it to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank, or put 2 favor on it to gain 1 secret per matching faceup adviser from the shared bank. Facedown advisers do not match. With no matching advisers, the second Trade option gains zero secrets, but its 2-favor cost remains payable. Finite favor/warband supplies limit gains to what is available; secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Muster — 1 Supply ... empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site ... gain 2 warbands. Trade — 1 Supply ... 1 secret → 1 favor plus matching advisers; 2 favor → 1 shared-bank secret per matching adviser; no matches means zero secrets; costs remain payable.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A relic must be facedown at your site; pay its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in your personal bank. A banner may be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank. To take People's Favor, pay strictly more favor than it currently holds and put the payment on it; distribute its old favor one at a time to suit banks, starting at any chosen bank and proceeding away from the world deck through the printed bank order, wrapping as needed. Do not return old favor to the previous holder; flip Mob to normal if applicable, and no seizure penalty applies. To take Darkest Secret, pay strictly more secrets than it holds; put the new payment on it, the new holder takes one old secret, and the previous holder takes the rest. If recovering it from yourself, return all old secrets to yourself; if from shared bank, the remainder stays there.
answers.evidence: Recover 1 facedown relic at your site or either banner from anywhere ... People's Favor ... strictly greater ... distribute old favor ... Darkest Secret ... strictly greater ... new holder takes 1 old secret, previous holder takes rest.

answers.answer: Another player's Darkest Secret is protected from Recover unless their pawn's site has at least one suited card whose suit matches none of that player's faceup advisers. One such mismatching card is enough even if other site cards match. If the holder has no faceup advisers but a suited site card exists, the card matches none of the advisers, so the banner is recoverable. An empty site or a ruin-only site has no suited card and protects the banner. Recovery from yourself or the shared bank ignores this protection.
answers.evidence: At least one suited card at their pawn’s site whose suit matches none of their faceup advisers. Empty sites and ruin-only sites protect it ... If holder has no faceup advisers but a suited site card exists, it is recoverable.

answers.answer: You may choose any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there as defender. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may additionally target any of that defender's sites anywhere on the map, with 1 defense die per site. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may also target any of their relics, banners, or their pawn and favor together; a relic uses its printed defense dice, a banner uses dice equal to its resources, and pawn plus favor uses 2 dice. A co-located defender's relic target itself satisfies the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Choose defender ... any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there ... at least one target ... at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you must target it ... may target any of defender's sites anywhere ... co-located relic target satisfies local-target requirement.

answers.answer: The attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in their board force. Defense is shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack), plus all defending warbands at targeted sites, plus the defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or any targeted site; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Battle plans and other applicable modifiers apply, and Oathkeeper/Usurper titles add a mandatory 1/2 defense die. Each skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords, then add one attack for each pair of hollow swords; an unpaired hollow sword adds zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but must sacrifice exactly enough to win and cannot sacrifice extra. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower is a defender victory. A defeated defender kills half its defending force rounded down; a defeated attacker kills half its remaining attacking force rounded down. Bandits cannot be killed.
answers.evidence: Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands ... defense shields plus site warbands plus eligible defender board force ... skulls kill own force; pairs of hollow swords add 1 ... sacrifice exactly enough to win ... strictly exceeds; tie or lower means defender wins.

answers.answer: On attacker victory, first the defender kills half the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, and returns the rest to board; resolve defeated battle-plan effects. Then the attacker may place any number, including zero, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites. With zero placed, a site is left to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners. A banner seized any way except Recover has 2 resources burned, to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn-and-favor was targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply and may separately burn half the defender's board favor rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker's destination choice if its enemy ruler chooses the forced destination. Then resolve attacker victorious battle-plan effects and discard plans that say “At end, discard.” If the attacker loses, skip target resolution and resolve defender victorious effects. Supremacy title transfers at Campaign end, not during temporary loss of site rule.
answers.evidence: Resolve defeat before taking targets ... may place any number, including zero ... Take all targeted relics/banners. For a seized banner ... burn 2 ... pawn-and-favor ... force defender to travel ... Finish battle-plan effects ... title transfer at end of Campaign.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. The defending side activates relevant modifiers and shares powers as one side for “you,” “your enemy,” and “defender,” but “your site” and “your board” still refer to each player's own. Allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. Defenders/Allies may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not other players' advisers; each shared plan can be used once total by one user who pays. The declared defender decides order, timing, and priority when Allies disagree. Chancellor selects Imperial defender casualties; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards remain there. A Citizen attacking the Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; likewise a Citizen attacked by the Chancellor is non-Imperial for it. This does not make all Citizens non-Imperial in an intra-Empire Campaign.
answers.evidence: When an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins as Ally ... share powers as one defending side ... each shared battle plan ... once total ... Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die ... only the specified attacker/defender loses that status temporarily.

answers.answer: Base Travel Supply costs by origin and destination region are: from Cradle, 1 to Cradle, 2 to Provinces, 4 to Hinterland; from Provinces, 2 to each region; from Hinterland, 4 to Cradle, 2 to Provinces, 3 to Hinterland. Travel may go to any different site, not only an adjacent one. Reveal a facedown destination and put its printed favor/secrets there from the shared bank and its printed number of facedown relics beside it from the relic deck. Apply fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases; any applicable free-Travel power is the final override and makes payment zero even if another power increases cost. Examples of modifiers: coast-to-coast costs 1 and ignores Narrow Pass; Charming Valley adds 1 when traveling from it; Shrouded Wood costs 2 when traveling from it and ignores Narrow Pass/Hidden Place. Site entry restrictions still apply unless ignored by a power.
answers.evidence: Travel cost matrix ... Reveal facedown destination; put printed favor/secrets and relics ... fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. Free Travel is the final override ... Site entry restrictions still apply unless ignored.

answers.answer: The Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, but cannot use its powers on the turn they took it. In a later turn, the offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; the parties may additionally negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. Acceptance flips the recipient to Citizen and replaces all their own board and map warbands with purple; if there is not enough purple, the new Citizen chooses which warbands to remove and replace. They discard their revealed Vision, flip Usurper to Oathkeeper, end their Act if it is their turn, and refresh to full leftmost Supply. They exchange promised pieces, and the Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. The offer cannot occur on the turn the current Scepter holder took it.
answers.evidence: Offer ... exactly one Reliquary relic; may additionally negotiate a binding exchange ... Acceptance: flip to Citizen; replace all own warbands ... discard revealed Vision, flip Usurper title ... exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains newly uncovered mandatory modifier.

answers.answer: For the next Oath, if victory came by Vision alone, choose the Oath matching that Vision. For any other single method or multiple victory methods, choose any Oath except the current one, and save that goal in the World Box. For Chronicle Citizenship, the Exile winner flips all Citizen boards, including boxed boards, to Exile, then may offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; no Reliquary relic, resource payment, or Scepter permission is required. Each accepting Exile flips to Citizen and replaces every garrison at every site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband per site. Rebuild the world deck with the top stack of 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 total), the middle stack of 15 denizens plus the other 3 Visions (18 total), and remaining denizens below. The Chronicle aid's “12 denizens + 2” is identified as incorrect; it would make 14 rather than the specified 12-card top stack.
answers.evidence: Vow an Oath ... Chronicle Citizenship ... flip all Citizen boards ... each accepting Exile ... exactly one winner-color warband at that site ... Rebuild ... top stack 10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12 ... aid's printed ‘12 denizens + 2’ is incorrect.
